note: First-line for any chest pain or syncope; look for ST elevation/depression, new T-wave inversion, or signs of right heart strain (PE).
Elevated in myocardial injury; a single normal troponin early after symptom onset does not exclude ACS.
High sensitivity, low specificity for PE/DVT; most useful to rule out PE in a low pre-test-probability patient, not to rule it in.
Definitive imaging for suspected pulmonary embolism when D-dimer is positive or pre-test probability is high.
Definitive imaging for suspected aortic dissection; order emergently if tearing pain with pulse/BP differential.
Elevated lactate suggests tissue hypoperfusion; used to risk-stratify suspected sepsis severity.
Confirms meningitis (CSF pleocytosis) or subarachnoid hemorrhage (xanthochromia) when CT head is negative but suspicion remains high.
First-line for suspected stroke, subarachnoid hemorrhage, or altered mental status of unclear cause.
Mandatory in any female of childbearing age with abdominal pain before further imaging or medication decisions.
Combined with glucose and ABG to confirm diabetic ketoacidosis (ketosis + metabolic acidosis + hyperglycemia).
Elevated 3x upper limit supports acute pancreatitis; imaging still needed to assess severity/complications.
Pyuria/nitrites support UTI; also screens for hematuria (stone) and glucose/ketones (metabolic causes).
